model_interpretation.claim: Changing the full-height pencil from 4x64 to 8x64 may improve x-direction global-load coalescing and halve the x block count. It also doubles threads per block to 512; occupancy effects could offset those gains. This isolates the wider-pencil/full-slab case without presuming a win over y-subtile tiling.

items.subject: Shared-memory pencil geometry: full-height versus y-subtile tiling
items.objective: Explore shared-memory pencil geometry as a contrast to the supplied 4-by-64 block. Compare wider x pencils while retaining the full 64-row y slab (for example, 8- or 16-wide x pencils) against x-wide blocks producing smaller y subtiles with radius-4 halos. Measure the tradeoff between improved x coalescing, block count, halo duplication, synchronization, and occupancy; do not assume either shape wins. Preserve the exact stencil coefficients and baseline y-halo/period-63 endpoint mapping, cover every output, validate against the independent oracle for varying signed inputs, and compare full-run event latency. Use only the existing buffers and allowed launch model.
